notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found for the 1985 currency-symbol exclusion list). §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11: literal-6 "must be nonnumeric and is limited to a single character", may be any character except the digits, "the uppercase letters A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z; the lowercase letters a through z; or the space" and * + - , . ; ( ) " = /, and without the clause only the currency sign is the PICTURE currency symbol. SpecialNamesBinder.SwitchBindCurrency binds the bare one-character form at every edition (CurrencyOperandOf refuses a numeric literal and a figurative constant, COBOL0892; a longer literal is COBOL0890), RegisterCurrency records the symbol, PictureAnalyzer.Analyze reads it in a PICTURE, FinalizeCurrencySigns keeps the currency sign as the default, and the 2002 WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrase is refused at 85 by VisitCurrencySignClause (COBOL0893). Probed right at 85: L, U, G, the colon and > as symbols (fixed and floating), the excluded digits, space, =, A and z refused (COBOL0891), PIC L99 without the clause refused (COBOL0808). PARTIAL because ValidateCurrencyChar holds ONE exclusion list, the 2023 one (§2023:12.3.7.3 SR22: A B C D E N P R S V X Z in either case), with no edition arm: (1) at --std 85 CURRENCY SIGN IS "E" and "N" are refused (COBOL0891) although the 1985 list has neither letter; (2) a lowercase letter outside that list ("m", "l") compiles at 85 although 1985 excludes every lowercase letter. Also seen, the format row's matter: two CURRENCY SIGN clauses in one paragraph compile at 85 (the 2002 form; §1985:VI.4.5.2 prints the clause once). The witness runs CURRENCY SIGN IS "L" with PIC L99.

next.reason: 1985 excludes 'uppercase letters A, B, C, D, P, R, S, V, X, Z; the lowercase letters a through z; or the space'. §2023:12.3.7.3 SR22 excludes 'alphabetic characters A, B, C, D, E, N, P, R, S, V, X, Z, or their lowercase equivalents', with equivalence per §2023:12.3.7.3 SR20. Stricter: CURRENCY SIGN 'E' or 'N' (legal in 1985) is refused. Looser: lowercase letters other than the listed ones (e.g. 'm') are accepted. 1985 'only the currency sign ... may be used' without the clause becomes §2023:12.3.7.3 SR25 (CURRENCY SIGN '$' implied unless some clause names '$', so '$' stays usable beside another currency sign). Literal class per §2023:12.3.7.3 SR18; PICTURE use per §2023:12.3.7.4 GR13. All compile-time.
